claims.text: The initial non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys are as-deposited materials produced by arc melting or melt spinning.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi alloy forms an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The baseline material has relatively coarse grains.
The baseline material contains significant internal residual stress.
The low surface-to-volume ratio of the bulk baseline limits its heat-exchange rate.
The bulk baseline undergoes a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Thin-film deposition at constant nominal composition will produce smaller grains than arc-melted or melt-spun material.
The thin-film intervention will increase grain-boundary and interfacial density.
Controlled thin-film deposition will reduce residual strain relative to the baseline.
A high density of defects can produce a broad distribution of exchange parameters and spatially inhomogeneous magnetic properties.
Reducing grain size while increasing interface density will make local magnetic exchange interactions more uniform.
More uniform local exchange interactions will smooth the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Smoothing the magnetostructural transition will broaden the magnetocaloric response curve.
Smoothing the magnetostructural transition will reduce hysteresis width.
The higher surface-to-volume ratio of thin films will promote faster heat exchange.
Faster heat exchange will mitigate the sharp entropy change and hysteresis.
Thin-film samples will have improved heat-exchange rates relative to the bulk baseline.
Thin-film samples will retain a similar or only slightly lower peak magnetic entropy change.
The proposed microstructural mechanism should operate under low applied fields near the transition temperature.
At very high fields or outside the immediate transition-temperature range, other effects may dominate the magnetocaloric response.

contradictions.description: The initial state is called 'as-deposited' while being defined as arc-melted or melt-spun material, whereas thin-film deposition is introduced as the intervention. This makes the identity of the requested as-deposited baseline internally inconsistent.
